extracted.intended_audience: researchers/authors submitting manuscripts to PLOS ONE
extracted.subtask_description: Journal-level publication criteria describing what kinds of manuscripts PLOS ONE will consider and the standards submissions must meet (scope, originality, methodological rigor, ethics, reporting, and language). Intended to guide authors preparing submissions and editors/reviewers assessing suitability.

rubrics_metrics.name: The study presents the results of primary scientific research.
rubrics_metrics.description: PLOS ONE is designed to communicate primary scientific research across the natural sciences, medical research, engineering, and related social sciences and humanities; submissions must present original primary research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The journal will not consider reviews, case reports, study protocols, hypothesis/proposal papers, letters/commentaries/essays, opinion pieces, policy papers, clinical practice guidelines, other secondary literature, or monographs. Occasionally commissioned Collection Reviews/Overviews are accepted only if solicited. Acceptable article types (with conditions) include: systematic reviews (only if methods ensure comprehensive and unbiased sampling of literature), submissions describing methods/software/databases/tools (if they follow appropriate reporting guidelines), qualitative research (only if it adheres to appropriate study design and reporting guidelines), and studies reporting negative results. See submission guidelines for discipline-specific requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results reported have not been published elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.description: PLOS ONE does not accept studies already published, in whole or in part, in the peer-reviewed literature; all figures should be original and not previously published; submissions under consideration elsewhere are not accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deposition in preprint servers (e.g., bioRxiv, arXiv), publication as a thesis, or conference presentation does not preclude consideration. Authors should not submit manuscripts simultaneously to multiple journals. For replication studies or submissions very similar to previous work, authors must provide a sound scientific rationale, clearly reference and discuss existing literature, and justify novelty/need; otherwise such submissions will likely be rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experiments, statistics, and other analyses are performed to a high technical standard and are described in sufficient detail.
rubrics_metrics.description: Experimental work, statistical analyses, and other methods must meet rigorous technical standards and be described so that others can reproduce the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experiments must be conducted with appropriate controls and replication. Sample sizes should be large enough to produce robust results where applicable. Methods and reagents must be described in sufficient detail for another researcher to reproduce the experiments. See submission guidelines for further methodological/reporting detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conclusions are presented in an appropriate fashion and are supported by the data.
rubrics_metrics.description: Conclusions drawn in the manuscript must be justified by the presented data and analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manuscripts will be rejected if interpretation of results is unjustified or inappropriate. Authors should avoid overstating conclusions. Discussion of possible implications is allowed provided such implications are clearly labeled as hypotheses rather than definitive conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: The article is presented in an intelligible fashion and is written in standard English.
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitted manuscripts must be clear, correct, and unambiguous in language because PLOS ONE does not copyedit accepted manuscripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Papers with poor or unclear language may be rejected. If language quality is poor, authors may be advised to seek independent editorial or manuscript-editing services prior to revision. Ensure readability and standard English usage throughout.

rubrics_metrics.name: The research meets all applicable standards for the ethics of experimentation and research integrity.
rubrics_metrics.description: Research must comply with high ethical standards for experimentation and publication integrity; the journal may apply standards more stringent than local requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ethics approvals/permissions are required for studies involving humans (including observational/survey-based studies or any personal data), animals (including observational animal studies), non-commercial cell lines, field sampling, and work with potential biosafety implications. If approval was not obtained, authors must explain why it was not required. PLOS ONE follows COPE Code of Conduct and Best Practice Guidelines; authors are expected to comply with publication ethics regarding authorship, dual publication, plagiarism, figure manipulation, and competing interests. Concerns should be raised with the editorial office.

rubrics_metrics.name: The article adheres to appropriate reporting guidelines and community standards for data availability.
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts must follow discipline-appropriate reporting guidelines and community standards for making data available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Results should be reported rigorously according to community/discipline standards (see submission guidelines for discipline-specific reporting guidance). Authors must follow standards for data deposition in publicly available resources (e.g., gene sequences, microarray expression, structural data). Failure to comply with community data-sharing standards may result in rejection. See PLOS ONE data availability policy for details.
